topology_reasoning.description: Two parallel curved waveguides with dense vertical grating/Bragg reflector pattern in the middle for mode coupling and wavelength selectivity
key_features: Top waveguide: curved S-taper entry on left, straight section, U-bend exit on right
Bottom waveguide: mirrored S-taper entry on left, straight section, tapered exit on right
Central region: dense vertical gratings (Bragg reflectors) spanning the coupling region
Symmetric layout with slight asymmetry in bends

functional_knobs.waveguide_width_um: Cross-sectional width of each waveguide - controls mode confinement and coupling strength
functional_knobs.grating_pitch_um: Spacing between vertical grating lines - controls Bragg wavelength and bandpass
functional_knobs.grating_length_um: Length of the grating region - controls interaction strength and bandwidth
functional_knobs.grating_depth_um: Etch depth of vertical gratings - controls coupling efficiency
functional_knobs.coupler_gap_um: Gap between top and bottom waveguides - controls supermode coupling length
functional_knobs.bend_radius_um: Radius of curvature for U-bends - affects adiabatic transition

knob_description: All top-level parameters are fully tunable and move real geometry. Device is parametric in all critical dimensions: waveguide_width_um, grating_pitch_um, grating_depth_um, grating_length_um, coupler_gap_um, and bend_radius_um. Changes to these knobs produce proportional changes in the generated GDS polygons.
implementation_notes: Device uses gdsfactory add_polygon() to create smooth, continuously-variable geometry without discretization. Centerlines are computed from parametric sine-wave functions, then offset by +/- waveguide_width_um/2 to create the actual polygons. Gratings are added as separate vertical rectangles positioned at regular intervals. No component stencils or pre-built cells used - pure primitives.
